changelog:
v5.2.5 — Search finds what you typed, and the app uses much less memory

• Search now shows the closest match first. Typing "Scream" puts Scream (1996) and its 4K copy at the top, instead of 60 older look-alikes.

• You can type the year after a title ("Scream 1996", "Doctor Who 2005") and Search understands it.

• Search ignores accents and punctuation, so "Jay Z" finds "JAŸ-Z in 8" and "Spider Man" finds "Spider-Man".

• The movie library grew to over 135,000 titles this month. The app now loads it in a lighter way, so Home, Movies and Search use far less memory, and the freezes some Fire TV Sticks saw after October 29 should stop.

• Very large categories show their first 3,000 titles with a note. Use the search icon at the top of the category to find anything in it.

• Adult categories are still there, but their titles no longer appear in Search, on Home, or in the Movies "By decade" rows.

• A live channel that reconnects on its own no longer triggers the slow-connection tip.
